candidates: When a refactoring in the `mermaid` package changes a publicly exported API shape (e.g., replacing an exported singleton object with a class export), determine whether the change is breaking for downstream consumers and classify the changeset in `.changeset/*.md` as `major` rather than `patch` if it is.

In class-based diagram database implementations (e.g., `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/<diagram>/db.ts`), manage all diagram state as direct class instance properties (e.g., `private nodes: Node[] = []`) rather than delegating to an `ImperativeState` wrapper or a separate plain-object state container. The class itself is the state container; `ImperativeState` is not needed in this pattern.

Do not assign imported functions to class members using arrow-function field syntax (e.g., `public setAccTitle = setAccTitle`). Older Safari versions have known compatibility issues with certain class field initializer expressions, and class methods are generally preferred over instance-bound arrow function fields for inherited or delegated behaviour.

Avoid `as TypeName` type assertions for type narrowing. At runtime, use an `instanceof` check and throw a descriptive `Error` (e.g., pointing to the project issue tracker) when the expected type is not satisfied. When a TypeScript type error is genuinely unavoidable at an initialization site, use `// @ts-expect-error: <descriptive reason>` rather than a cast.

Diagram DB classes in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/` do not need to initialize or reset state in their constructor. The Mermaid `Diagram` class automatically calls `db.clear?.()` before each parse cycle, so all state initialization and reset logic belongs only in the `clear()` method.
